## Design

### 2026-10-18 – Spent 3 hours designing and finalising the custom two-part enclosure for the handheld cyberdeck in Tinkercad. The top shell was constructed on a 92 mm x 67 mm base plate with a 15mm  thickness, featur

**5h**

Spent 3 hours designing and finalising the custom two-part enclosure for the handheld cyberdeck in Tinkercad. The top shell was constructed on a 92 mm x 67 mm base plate with a 15mm  thickness, featuring precise cutouts for the 2.4" TFT display active window , an 8x8 LED matrix, dual push buttons, and a front rotary encoder cutout designed to hang slightly off the bottom edge for easy thumb control. The matching bottom tray was hollowed out with 2mm walls to house the dual-board stackup and LiPo battery, complete with an  floor cutout for the ESP32 camera lens and a side-wall slot engineered to let a flat disc thumbwheel potentiometer protrude by 6mm for smooth volume control. Both primary components were grouped, verified for clearance tolerances, and prepared as separate STL files ready for 3D printing.

### 2026-10-18 – Continued the CAD session by designing and finalizing the matching bottom tray enclosure to house the internal hardware stackup. A 2mm wall thickness was maintained around a hollow interior cavity siz

**2h**

Continued the CAD session by designing and finalizing the matching bottom tray enclosure to house the internal hardware stackup. A 2mm wall thickness was maintained around a hollow interior cavity sized specifically to fit the dual-board PCB stack, LiPo battery, and power routing. Cut a targeted 8.5mm aperture into the bottom floor to align cleanly with the ESP32 camera module lens, and added a side-wall slot engineered for a flat disc thumbwheel potentiometer to protrude by approximately 6mm for easy volume adjustment. With both top and bottom enclosure pieces fully hollowed, cut out, and verified for assembly fitment, the CAD models were grouped and prepared for individual STL export for 3D printing.

### 2026-10-18 – Over a 5-hour CAD session in Tinkercad, I designed, refined, and validated the complete two-part enclosure for the OutBound handheld cyberdeck. The top shell was constructed on a custom base plate wit

**5h**

Over a 5-hour CAD session in Tinkercad, I designed, refined, and validated the complete two-part enclosure for the OutBound handheld cyberdeck. The top shell was constructed on a custom base plate with tailored wall thickness, featuring precise cutouts for the TFT display, LED matrix, dual push buttons, and a front-edge rotary encoder clearance cutout designed to hang slightly off the front for easy thumb access. The matching bottom tray was engineered with reinforced walls around a hollow interior cavity tailored to fit the dual-board PCB stack, LiPo battery, and power routing, featuring a targeted floor aperture for the camera module lens and a side-wall slot permitting a flat disc thumbwheel potentiometer to protrude for smooth volume control. To conclude the session, both models were grouped, converted into an editable .step CAD source format alongside individual .stl files for 3D printing, and committed directly to the Humaid-Alvi12/OutBound GitHub repository to successfully pass the Haflife submission validation checks.

### 2026-10-18 – Spent 4 hours refining the enclosure design, optimizing tolerances, and converting the CAD models for open-source repository submission. Adjusted the internal mounting layout for the dual-board stack,

**5h**

Spent 4 hours refining the enclosure design, optimizing tolerances, and converting the CAD models for open-source repository submission. Adjusted the internal mounting layout for the dual-board stack, LiPo battery, and display alignment, ensuring smooth assembly clearances for the camera aperture and side-wall thumbwheel slot. Generated and verified the editable .step CAD source file from Tinkercad to complement the printable .stl exports, then committed the updated assets to the GitHub repository to fulfill the Haflife source validation checks.
